name: Nursing Patient Education & Discharge Teaching
description: Evaluates a nurse teaching a patient or family member about a medication, device, or discharge plan in plain English, and confirming understanding with a teach-back.

anchors.80-100: Clear, fluent, unhurried phrasing at a pace a worried patient can follow.
anchors.50-70: Understandable but occasional hesitations or grammar errors interrupt the explanation.
anchors.10-40: Frequent errors that leave the patient unsure what they were told.

anchors.80-100: Replaces jargon with everyday words, or defines a term immediately when it must be used.
anchors.50-70: Mixes plain language with unexplained clinical terms.
anchors.10-40: Explains in clinical register the patient cannot be expected to understand.

anchors.80-100: Chunks the content, signposts each step, and orders it by what the patient must do first.
anchors.50-70: Covers the content but in one long block, or in an order that follows the chart rather than the patient's day.
anchors.10-40: Unstructured; key actions are scattered or never separated from background detail.

anchors.80-100: Asks the patient to say the plan back in their own words, and corrects gaps without blaming them.
anchors.50-70: Asks 'do you understand?' or 'any questions?' but never has the patient demonstrate.
anchors.10-40: Never checks understanding, or accepts a nod as confirmation.

anchors.80-100: Names the specific warning signs, what to do about each, and who to contact.
anchors.50-70: Mentions warning signs generally ('if you feel unwell, call us').
anchors.10-40: No safety net, or omits a warning sign the case makes essential.

anchors.80-100: Acknowledges the patient's worry or difficulty, invites questions, and stays warm throughout.
anchors.50-70: Polite but transactional; the patient's stated concern goes unaddressed.

checklist.item: Checked what the patient already knows or is worried about before teaching
Explained the key information in plain English, without unexplained jargon
Stated concretely what the patient must do, and when
Named the specific warning signs and what to do if they occur
Asked the patient to repeat the plan back in their own words (teach-back)
Corrected any gap in the teach-back without blaming the patient
Invited questions and confirmed who to contact
